title: Does half a lens make half a picture?
hook: Cover the top half of a camera lens.

knows: the quantities named in the question
doesNotKnow: Light from each object point can reach the image through different parts of the lens. Covering half blocks some rays from each point; it does not select half the picture.

misconception: The alternative answers in the prediction appear plausible without the stated physical model.
objective: Light from each object point can reach the image through different parts of the lens. Covering half blocks some rays from each point; it does not select half the picture.

claims.text: Light from each object point can reach the image through different parts of the lens. Covering half blocks some rays from each point; it does not select half the picture. Ideal geometric optics: a focused image, uniform illumination, and diffraction neglected.
claims.source: Thin-lens geometric optics: rays from each object point through different lens positions converge at the conjugate image point.

recall.question: You partly cover a focused projector lens. In the geometric-optics model, what happens to the screen picture?
recall.why: Each part of the lens contributes light to the whole focused image.
